description: 20 distinct 60-question Language papers and 20 distinct 15-question practice sets, original content with 317-word spelling bank. Automated answer and uniqueness checks passed. Human editorial spot checks conducted; continued review recommended.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Neither the chair nor the analysts who drafted the report ___ prepared to endorse it.
options: has been
were
was
is
questions.explanation: The nearer plural noun requires the plural verb were.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Each of the findings that the analysts discussed ___ supported by independent evidence.
options: were
have been
is
are
questions.explanation: The singular distributive head each governs is despite the intervening plural phrase.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: By the time Anika presented the report, the review team ___ its sources.
options: has already checked
will check
is checking
had already checked
questions.explanation: Past perfect marks a completed event before another past event.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: After reviewing the contradictory evidence, ___.
options: the analysts revised their interpretation
a discrepancy became apparent
the report was amended
the result seemed doubtful
questions.explanation: The people who performed the reviewing must immediately follow the opening modifier.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: The revised interpretation was more comprehensive than ___.
options: the archive that stored the document
that in the earlier report
the previous chair
the original analysts
questions.explanation: The construction compares interpretations with interpretations, not people or institutions.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: If Anika ___ responsible for the report, the chair would seek independent confirmation.
options: has been
is
were
will be
questions.explanation: Were expresses an unreal present condition in conventional formal usage.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: The report may be accepted only if the analysts approve it. What can be inferred?
options: Their approval guarantees acceptance.
Acceptance may precede approval under the stated rule.
No unapproved proposal has ever been submitted.
Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
questions.explanation: Only if specifies a necessary condition and does not guarantee success.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Anika as the person who actually inspected the evidence?
options: After inspecting the evidence, Anika informed the chair.
Anika informed the chair after she inspected it.
After she inspected it, Anika informed the chair.
The chair and Anika discussed the findings after she inspected it.
questions.explanation: The introductory modifier clearly identifies its agent in the first sentence; the other references are ambiguous.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which sentence means that the analysts revised no section except the conclusion?
options: The analysts revised the only conclusion of the report.
The analysts revised only the conclusion of the report.
Only the analysts revised the conclusion of the report.
The analysts only revised the conclusion of the report.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?
options: The report was persuasive; nevertheless the chair requested more evidence.
The report was persuasive nevertheless; the chair requested more evidence.
The report was persuasive; nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The report was persuasive, nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates the independent clauses and a comma follows nevertheless.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: The number of analysts assigned to the task ___ increased since September.
options: have
were
are
has
questions.explanation: The singular head number takes has, despite the plural noun in its complement.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which version accurately compares the number of unsupported claims?
options: The revised report contained fewer unsupported claims.
The revised report contained less unsupported claims.
The revised report contained least unsupported claims.
The revised report contained much fewer unsupported claims.
questions.explanation: Claims are countable, so fewer is the standard comparative.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
options: The sketch is more colorful than the old one.
If I was Noah, I would take more notes.
Because Mateo forgot the photograph, we returned home.
No mistakes.
questions.explanation: Sentence B contains the error. Were expresses a contrary-to-fact hypothetical condition. Corrected sentence: If I were Noah, I would take more notes.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
options: Nora carried glue, paper, and scissors to the weather presentation.
The researchers were eager to sing, to dance, and to paint.
Sofia is laying on the grass after the museum tour.
No mistakes.
questions.explanation: Sentence C contains the error. Lie means recline; its -ing form is lying. Corrected sentence: Sofia is lying on the grass after the museum tour.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
options: The price of the letters will raise next month.
There were three options: repair, replace, or return.
The cooking class began, so we found our seats.
No mistakes.
questions.explanation: Sentence A contains the error. Rise describes an increase without a direct object. Corrected sentence: The price of the letters will rise next month.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
options: The team performed well at the trail cleanup.
The athletes have went to the school tournament.
The bridge design contest takes place in May.
No mistakes.
questions.explanation: Sentence B contains the error. After have, use the past participle gone. Corrected sentence: The athletes have gone to the school tournament.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
options: The museum tour begins on Monday.
The analysts discussed the weather presentation.
The panel performed good at the writing workshop.
No mistakes.
questions.explanation: Sentence C contains the error. Use well to modify performed. Corrected sentence: The panel performed well at the writing workshop.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?

The readers speak English at the library festival.

questions.explanation: Sentence B contains the error. Avoid combining more with an -er comparative. Corrected sentence: This poster is smaller than the other one.

questions.explanation: Sentence C contains the error. An adverb modifies how an action is performed. Corrected sentence: The gardeners completed the work carefully.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?

The robotics demonstration begins on monday.

questions.explanation: Sentence C contains the error. Capitalize the name of a day of the week. Corrected sentence: The robotics demonstration begins on Monday.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?

questions.explanation: Sentence B contains the error. Place a comma after the introductory dependent clause. Corrected sentence: When the reading challenge ended, we went home.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
options: The committee made an honest effort.

The students enjoyed the show, they applauded.

questions.explanation: Sentence C contains the error. A semicolon correctly joins independent clauses. Corrected sentence: The students enjoyed the show; they applauded.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
options: Mateo saw a unusual photograph at the art exhibition.
One of the plants is missing from the display.
The performers have gone to the music rehearsal.

questions.explanation: Sentence A contains the error. Unusual starts with a vowel sound. Corrected sentence: Mateo saw an unusual photograph at the art exhibition.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
options: Neither Keira nor the librarians were ready.
Because Lina forgot the sample.
The journalists didn't go to the newspaper meeting.

questions.explanation: Sentence B contains the error. A because-clause alone is a fragment. Corrected sentence: Because Lina forgot the sample, we returned home.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
options: Neither Elena nor the students were ready.
Esme has written an account of the robotics demonstration.
Hana likes reading, sketching, and to dance at the cooking class.

questions.explanation: Sentence C contains the error. Keep list items parallel. Corrected sentence: Hana likes reading, sketching, and dancing at the cooking class.

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
options: Walking to the bridge design contest, Aisha dropped the sketch.
The news about the art exhibition is encouraging.
Tomorrow, the research team will finish its work.

questions.explanation: None of the three sentences contains a grammar, usage, or punctuation error. Choice D is correct.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: A preliminary observation in astronomy was positive. Which conclusion is appropriately calibrated?
options: One positive result demonstrates a permanent causal mechanism.
The evidence is encouraging, but different settings should be tested before generalizing.
The observation proves the technique works everywhere.
All alternative explanations are now impossible.
questions.explanation: A preliminary observation supports a provisional inference rather than a universal conclusion.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which evidence would best establish that a new procedure reduced errors in astronomy?
options: A description of the room where the procedure originated.
The number of pages in the final report.
A comparison of verified error rates under comparable conditions.
An announcement praising the procedure's designers.
questions.explanation: Comparable error-rate measurements directly test the alleged improvement.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which sentence makes a concession without abandoning the argument?
options: The intervention costs money, so the idea must be rejected.
The intervention cannot possibly have drawbacks.
The intervention is correct because its supporters are enthusiastic.
Although implementation may be costly, a limited pilot could test whether the benefits justify that expense.
questions.explanation: The concession admits a legitimate cost while proposing evidence to evaluate the trade-off.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in astronomy?
options: Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which transition best introduces a limitation following positive results?
options: Similarly, no further investigation is necessary.
Nevertheless, the data cover too short a period to establish a lasting trend.
Therefore, every other hypothesis is impossible.
In other words, a favorable result guarantees universal success.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a meaningful qualification to apparently promising evidence.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in astronomy?
options: Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: A paragraph explains community choir and notes: 'During the final rehearsal, singers entered together more consistently.' Which ending best restates its larger point?
options: This paragraph has reached its last sentence.
A community choir improved its performance by responding to shared cues.
The park installed new drinking fountains.
Some singers missed the conductor's signal at a quiet entrance.
questions.explanation: A conclusion returns to the central idea instead of adding an irrelevant or isolated detail.

questions.text: Choose a transition: 'A dry spell left the garden soil cracked. ____ By autumn, the class had enough observations for a science display.'
options: However,
Therefore,
For example,
Likewise,
questions.explanation: However signals a contrast between an initial obstacle and a positive result.

questions.text: Choose a transition: 'Several players entered a fast section at different moments. ____ The conductor slowed the passage and practiced it in small groups.'
options: In contrast,
For instance,
Meanwhile,
Therefore,
questions.explanation: Therefore introduces a response or result prompted by the earlier problem.

questions.text: The topic sentence is: 'A recycling campaign worked best when students tracked what actually changed.' Which sentence gives the clearest concrete example?
options: There are many interesting things to learn about the recycling campaign.
Someone said the idea sounded interesting.
The collection bins contained less mixed trash after students posted clear sorting instructions.
A classroom aquarium held several colorful fish.
questions.explanation: The specific observation illustrates the topic sentence.

questions.text: Choose the clearest revision of: 'The group made advance preparations ahead of time for the robotics workshop project.'
options: The group was at the point of planning preparations.
The group prepared for the robotics workshop project.
The group made preparations in advance ahead of time.
In advance, preparations were prepared by the group.
questions.explanation: The concise revision eliminates repeated expressions without losing meaning.

questions.text: In a paragraph about food pantry, which sentence introduces a problem that needs a response?
options: Some delivery boxes contained too many of one item and too few of another.
More families received balanced food packages.
The town clock was repaired last spring.
Volunteers tracked which staples ran low and updated their weekly packing list.
questions.explanation: The statement names the obstacle to be addressed.

questions.text: Which sentence best explains how the participants responded to this problem: 'New riders frequently forgot to look behind them before turning.'?
options: A nearby theater offered discounted tickets.
The project had started before this problem.
People sometimes enjoy community projects.
Instructors repeated the signaling exercises on a quiet course.
questions.explanation: A relevant solution directly addresses the stated problem.

questions.text: A paragraph says: 'Volunteers initially mixed all collected litter into one bag.' and ends with 'The final tally helped organizers plan future cleanup efforts.' Which sentence best connects the two?
options: Volunteers marked a safe stretch of beach.
There are many interesting things to learn about the beach cleanup.
They sorted items by type before weighing them.
The library hosted a poetry reading.
questions.explanation: The missing sentence should explain the intervention between the challenge and result.

questions.text: Read: 'Museum volunteers practiced explaining exhibits to visitors of different ages. After revisions, younger visitors could describe the experiment in their own words.' Which summary captures the main idea without focusing on one minor fact?
options: No clear conclusion about the topic is possible.
Museum volunteers practiced explaining exhibits to visitors of different ages.
After revisions, younger visitors could describe the experiment in their own words.
A delivery van waited outside the museum.
questions.explanation: A suitable summary expresses the whole idea rather than only one detail.

questions.text: Which fact would best support a paragraph arguing that oral-history project produced observable results?
options: A recorded interview described how the town's market had changed over decades.
There are many interesting things to learn about the oral-history project.
The music room purchased a piano bench.
The organizers thought their work was important.
questions.explanation: Measured or observed results are stronger support than broad opinions.

questions.text: A writer wants to keep a paragraph focused on the library book drive. Which sentence should be deleted?
options: Volunteers sorted the titles and added clear category stickers.
Volunteers organized donated books by reading level and delivered boxes to two community rooms.
The neighborhood book drive made reading materials easier to share.
A nearby bakery introduced a new blueberry muffin.
questions.explanation: The unrelated sentence diverts attention from the paragraph's focus.

questions.text: A paragraph contains these sentences: 'Some early arguments relied on unsupported guesses. The team added citations and practiced responding to questions. The final debate became more precise and persuasive.' What organizational structure is used?
options: A list of historical dates
A set of definitions for technical terms
Problem followed by solution and result
Comparison of two unrelated characters
questions.explanation: The paragraph introduces an obstacle, explains a response, and describes its outcome.

questions.text: Which sentence would most effectively introduce an essay about the weather station?
options: A month of recordings showed that afternoon temperatures varied more than students expected.
A school weather station helped students distinguish daily observations from longer-term patterns.
There are a lot of things about this topic.
The drama club ordered costumes for its play.
questions.explanation: An opening should present the controlling idea clearly and broadly enough for the paragraph.

questions.text: Choose the combination that best shows cause and response: 'The original plot offered flowers for only a short period.' 'Gardeners added plants that bloom at different times.'
options: Because the original plot offered flowers for only a short period, gardeners added plants that bloom at different times.
The original plot offered flowers for only a short period. Gardeners added plants that bloom at different times.
The original plot offered flowers for only a short period, gardeners added plants that bloom at different times.
Because gardeners added plants that bloom at different times, the original plot offered flowers for only a short period.
questions.explanation: Because introduces the reason for the response without reversing the causal relationship or creating a comma splice.

questions.text: In the day 7 ecology full-paper case: A preliminary observation in ecology was positive. Which conclusion is appropriately calibrated?
options: The observation proves the technique works everywhere.
All alternative explanations are now impossible.
One positive result demonstrates a permanent causal mechanism.
The evidence is encouraging, but different settings should be tested before generalizing.
questions.explanation: A preliminary observation supports a provisional inference rather than a universal conclusion.

questions.text: In the day 7 ecology full-paper case: Which evidence would best establish that a new procedure reduced errors in ecology?
options: A comparison of verified error rates under comparable conditions.
An announcement praising the procedure's designers.
A description of the room where the procedure originated.
The number of pages in the final report.
questions.explanation: Comparable error-rate measurements directly test the alleged improvement.

questions.text: In the day 7 ecology full-paper case: Which sentence makes a concession without abandoning the argument?
options: The intervention is correct because its supporters are enthusiastic.
Although implementation may be costly, a limited pilot could test whether the benefits justify that expense.
The intervention costs money, so the idea must be rejected.
The intervention cannot possibly have drawbacks.
questions.explanation: The concession admits a legitimate cost while proposing evidence to evaluate the trade-off.

questions.text: In the day 7 ecology full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in ecology?
options: Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: In the day 7 ecology full-paper case: Which transition best introduces a limitation following positive results?
options: Therefore, every other hypothesis is impossible.
In other words, a favorable result guarantees universal success.
Similarly, no further investigation is necessary.
Nevertheless, the data cover too short a period to establish a lasting trend.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a meaningful qualification to apparently promising evidence.

questions.text: In the day 7 ecology full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in ecology?
options: An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: Which sentence best explains how the participants responded to this problem: 'The first demonstration relied on unfamiliar technical terms.'?
options: A delivery van waited outside the museum.
The project had started before this problem.
People sometimes enjoy community projects.
The volunteers replaced jargon with simple descriptions and examples.
questions.explanation: A relevant solution directly addresses the stated problem.

questions.text: A paragraph says: 'The first interview questions encouraged only yes-or-no responses.' and ends with 'The recordings preserved details that short surveys had missed.' Which sentence best connects the two?
options: Students prepared open-ended interview questions.
There are many interesting things to learn about the oral-history project.
Students rewrote the questions to invite longer explanations.
The music room purchased a piano bench.
questions.explanation: The missing sentence should explain the intervention between the challenge and result.

questions.text: Read: 'The neighborhood book drive made reading materials easier to share. Volunteers organized donated books by reading level and delivered boxes to two community rooms.' Which summary captures the main idea without focusing on one minor fact?
options: No clear conclusion about the topic is possible.
The neighborhood book drive made reading materials easier to share.
Volunteers organized donated books by reading level and delivered boxes to two community rooms.
A nearby bakery introduced a new blueberry muffin.
questions.explanation: A suitable summary expresses the whole idea rather than only one detail.

questions.text: Which fact would best support a paragraph arguing that debate club produced observable results?
options: Members revised their speeches after checking the sources behind each statistic.
There are many interesting things to learn about the debate club.
The school gym received a new clock.
The organizers thought their work was important.
questions.explanation: Measured or observed results are stronger support than broad opinions.

questions.text: A writer wants to keep a paragraph focused on the weather station. Which sentence should be deleted?
options: Students secured the equipment and checked it after storms.
A month of recordings showed that afternoon temperatures varied more than students expected.
A school weather station helped students distinguish daily observations from longer-term patterns.
The drama club ordered costumes for its play.
questions.explanation: The unrelated sentence diverts attention from the paragraph's focus.

questions.text: A paragraph contains these sentences: 'The original plot offered flowers for only a short period. Gardeners added plants that bloom at different times. Pollinators could find flowers across a longer part of the season.' What organizational structure is used?
options: A list of historical dates
A set of definitions for technical terms
Problem followed by solution and result
Comparison of two unrelated characters
questions.explanation: The paragraph introduces an obstacle, explains a response, and describes its outcome.

questions.text: Which sentence would most effectively introduce an essay about the school newspaper?
options: Editors caught an incorrect date before the issue was printed.
A student newspaper improved when writers checked facts and organized their ideas.
There are a lot of things about this topic.
The art room installed additional shelves.
questions.explanation: An opening should present the controlling idea clearly and broadly enough for the paragraph.

questions.text: Choose the combination that best shows cause and response: 'Several teams began before measuring their ingredients.' 'The judges encouraged teams to prepare ingredients before cooking.'
options: Because several teams began before measuring their ingredients, the judges encouraged teams to prepare ingredients before cooking.
Several teams began before measuring their ingredients. The judges encouraged teams to prepare ingredients before cooking.
Several teams began before measuring their ingredients, the judges encouraged teams to prepare ingredients before cooking.
Because the judges encouraged teams to prepare ingredients before cooking, several teams began before measuring their ingredients.
questions.explanation: Because introduces the reason for the response without reversing the causal relationship or creating a comma splice.

questions.text: Which sentence best replaces the vague statement, 'The trail mapping team project did many important things' ?
options: The project included various activities that were activities.
The school bake sale featured cinnamon rolls.
There are several things to mention about the work.
A trail mapping team learned to verify landmarks rather than rely on memory.
questions.explanation: Precise writing identifies what was accomplished rather than saying only that things occurred.

questions.text: Which sentence is best described as the RESULT of the work in this passage? 'The first filter allowed water to flow through too quickly. Students changed the layers and repeated the experiment. The final prototype performed more consistently in repeated trials.'
options: A nearby farm grew sunflowers.
Students sketched a proposed invention.
The final prototype performed more consistently in repeated trials.
The first filter allowed water to flow through too quickly.
questions.explanation: The result occurs after the response and describes what changed.

questions.text: Read this paragraph draft: 'A student water-testing club used repeated measurements to understand changes in a local stream. Heavy rain made the stream cloudy for several days. ____ Club members collected additional water samples after the rain.' Which connector best links the problem to the response?
options: In the same way,
To address this problem,
By contrast,
For example,
questions.explanation: To address this problem explicitly explains the response to the obstacle.

questions.text: Which is the strongest topic sentence for a paragraph about community mural?
options: A neighborhood mural project helped residents share memories through art.
The final painting included designs suggested by children, shopkeepers, and longtime residents.
There are many interesting things to learn about the community mural.
A delivery truck arrived before sunrise.
questions.explanation: A focused topic sentence states the controlling idea rather than one detail or an unrelated fact.

questions.text: Which sentence is the strongest specific evidence supporting this claim? A history exhibit used everyday objects to explain changes in the town.
options: The basketball team practiced after school.
There are many interesting things to learn about the local history exhibit.
The organizers were excited at first.
Visitors compared an old railway ticket with a modern transit pass.
questions.explanation: Specific observations provide stronger support than vague statements or unrelated information.

questions.text: Consider a paragraph about stage production: (1) A theater crew discovered that rehearsing transitions is as important as practicing dialogue. (2) The final dress rehearsal had fewer delays between scenes. (3) The science lab ordered new safety goggles. (4) The performance moved smoothly from one scene to the next. Which numbered sentence should be removed?
options: Sentence 2
Sentence 4
Sentence 3
Sentence 1
questions.explanation: Sentence 3 shifts to an unrelated subject and breaks paragraph unity.

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: Neither the chair nor the analysts who drafted the report ___ prepared to endorse it.

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: The report may be accepted only if the analysts approve it. What can be inferred?

No unapproved proposal has ever been submitted.

Their approval guarantees acceptance.

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Tara as the person who actually inspected the evidence?

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: Which sentence means that the analysts revised no section except the conclusion?

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?

The report was persuasive; nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.

The report was persuasive; nevertheless the chair requested more evidence.

questions.text: In the day 16 journalism full-paper case: A preliminary observation in journalism was positive. Which conclusion is appropriately calibrated?
options: The evidence is encouraging, but different settings should be tested before generalizing.
The observation proves the technique works everywhere.
All alternative explanations are now impossible.
One positive result demonstrates a permanent causal mechanism.
questions.explanation: A preliminary observation supports a provisional inference rather than a universal conclusion.

questions.text: In the day 16 journalism full-paper case: Which evidence would best establish that a new procedure reduced errors in journalism?
options: The number of pages in the final report.

An announcement praising the procedure's designers.
A description of the room where the procedure originated.
questions.explanation: Comparable error-rate measurements directly test the alleged improvement.

questions.text: In the day 16 journalism full-paper case: Which sentence makes a concession without abandoning the argument?
options: The intervention cannot possibly have drawbacks.
The intervention is correct because its supporters are enthusiastic.
Although implementation may be costly, a limited pilot could test whether the benefits justify that expense.
The intervention costs money, so the idea must be rejected.
questions.explanation: The concession admits a legitimate cost while proposing evidence to evaluate the trade-off.

questions.text: In the day 16 journalism full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in journalism?
options: Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: In the day 16 journalism full-paper case: Which transition best introduces a limitation following positive results?
options: Nevertheless, the data cover too short a period to establish a lasting trend.
Therefore, every other hypothesis is impossible.

Similarly, no further investigation is necessary.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a meaningful qualification to apparently promising evidence.

questions.text: In the day 16 journalism full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in journalism?
options: A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.

Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

The finished mural represented more perspectives than the original proposal.
Several early sketches overlooked the area's history.

questions.text: In the day 19 psychology full-paper case: A preliminary observation in psychology was positive. Which conclusion is appropriately calibrated?
options: The observation proves the technique works everywhere.
All alternative explanations are now impossible.
One positive result demonstrates a permanent causal mechanism.
The evidence is encouraging, but different settings should be tested before generalizing.
questions.explanation: A preliminary observation supports a provisional inference rather than a universal conclusion.

questions.text: In the day 19 psychology full-paper case: Which evidence would best establish that a new procedure reduced errors in psychology?
options: A comparison of verified error rates under comparable conditions.
An announcement praising the procedure's designers.
A description of the room where the procedure originated.
The number of pages in the final report.
questions.explanation: Comparable error-rate measurements directly test the alleged improvement.

questions.text: In the day 19 psychology full-paper case: Which sentence makes a concession without abandoning the argument?
options: The intervention is correct because its supporters are enthusiastic.
Although implementation may be costly, a limited pilot could test whether the benefits justify that expense.
The intervention costs money, so the idea must be rejected.
The intervention cannot possibly have drawbacks.
questions.explanation: The concession admits a legitimate cost while proposing evidence to evaluate the trade-off.

questions.text: In the day 19 psychology full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in psychology?
options: Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: In the day 19 psychology full-paper case: Which transition best introduces a limitation following positive results?
options: Therefore, every other hypothesis is impossible.
In other words, a favorable result guarantees universal success.
Similarly, no further investigation is necessary.
Nevertheless, the data cover too short a period to establish a lasting trend.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a meaningful qualification to apparently promising evidence.

questions.text: In the day 19 psychology full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in psychology?
options: An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.
